Finding: Maximum Sharpe generated the strongest out-of-sample CAGR and Sharpe ratio.
Limitation: Maximum Sharpe had the highest turnover and largest maximum drawdown.

Finding: Minimum Volatility reduced annualised risk but did not improve realised returns.
Limitation: Lower volatility did not guarantee a smaller drawdown during prolonged market weakness.

Finding: Risk Parity provided the most balanced risk allocation and broad diversification.
Limitation: Its return and Sharpe remained below the current portfolio and Maximum Sharpe.

Finding: No optimisation method dominated across all realised stress periods.
Evidence: Maximum Sharpe won three stress windows; Minimum Volatility won two.
Limitation: Stress-period leadership was dependent on crisis type and duration.

Finding: Maximum Sharpe had the lowest simulated one-year probability of loss.
Limitation: Simulation results depend on historical blocks and shrunk expected-return assumptions.

Finding: The complete optimisation and risk pipeline works for arbitrary NSE and BSE portfolios.
Evidence: Validated using a six-stock portfolio with weight, amount and quantity input support.
Limitation: Stocks require sufficient aligned historical price observations.
